rationale: Single-process, single-GPU FP32 ResNet-18 batch-32 inference; the frozen objective is the process's torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() per repeat (request.json note: PyTorch allocated peak, not reserved/device-wide) subject to images_per_second >= 0.95x baseline. The torch collector already ran and its trace evidence is complete: 157/157 CUDA kernels associated below project, 0 unassociated, 0 root-only, 0 ambiguous forward sequences, 0 autograd ranges (coverage.json), so no overlap, graph-tracing or attribution question remains for nsys or execution_timeline to resolve. Communication capability is observed not_applicable ('single-device task', observations.json) and the forward contains no collectives, so nccl_tuning, collective_calibration and the PCIe/collective dimensions of device_telemetry are not applicable; NVML device-wide utilization/memory readings also cannot attribute the process-level allocated peak. python_runtime perturbs execution and yields no clean memory or GPU timing signal, with no host-bound evidence in the trace. candidate_diagnostics and binding_cost are not applicable before any candidate exists and can be requested in later candidate/feedback revisions (binding_cost would then also run in candidate resource feedback if selected). The evidence this objective needs - per-repeat peak_allocated_bytes, images_per_second and the fully attributed forward structure - is already supplied by the evaluator samples and the completed torch trace, so no additional collectors are requested and unavailable dimensions are listed with observed reasons rather than approximated.
